question:
Choose the idiom/phrase that can substitute the highlighted group of words meaningfully.

All the boys of this band are **similar in many ways.**
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"Birds of a feather"** means people **who have similar interests, ideas, or characteristics tend to associate with each other. (**एक जैसे लोग साथ रहते हैं)

 
 
• **Example:** **Birds of a feather** flock together; all the artists in the city seem to know each other.
 
 
 
• **"Similar"** refers to having characteristics in common. (समान)
 
 
• **Example:** The two brothers are very similar in their tastes and preferences.
 
 

Hence, we can infer that the idiom **"Birds of a feather"** fits well to describe people **who are similar in many ways**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Eats like a bird** (बहुत कम खाना): To eat very little.

 
 
• **Example:** She **eats like a bird**, barely touching her food at the dinner table.
 
 
 
• **A piece of cake** (बहुत आसान): Something very easy to do.
 
 
• **Example:** The math test was **a piece of cake **for her.
 
 
 
• **Flocking birds** (समूह में पक्षी): Refers to birds gathering in a group, not commonly used as an idiom.
 
 
• **Example:** We saw a group of **flocking birds** near the lake.
